understand.notes: DESIGN PATTERN ISSUE: The console was deliberately built conservative (shipped 2026-06-21) to avoid reflow risk mid-game. MobileScoreMirror is a glance-only read-out; all controls live in MobileScoreDock below. On desktop, the 3-column ScoreTile layout (HOME | CLOCK | AWAY) shows EVERY interactive control at once. On mobile, the mirror + dock split these visually, assuming the operator's eyes bounce between them. THE OPERATOR'S COMPLAINT: the void is demoralizing + the dock is tiny (one-handed thumb zone). SOLUTION VECTORS: (1) FULL-SCREEN DOCK: make MobileScoreDock fill the flex-1 region (not pinned); let dock scroll if device is short. (2) HORIZONTAL MOBILE TILES: render the 3 desktop ScoreTiles horizontally-scrollable on mobile (showcase the full board and controls, not just a mirror). (3) CONDENSED CHROME: shrink pills/status row from 164px to 100px to buy space. (4) LAZY RIBBON: hide RunRibbonPreview by default on mobile (operator presses 'Show' if needed); runway is 160px when visible. (5) COLLAPSIBLE ROSTER/CUES: already collapsed by default (rostbar = 48px closed), but cue bar is always 80px. Option: roll cues into the dock or hide under a 'More' menu. GROUNDING: the operator's phone is iPhone 14/15 (390×844, ~650px usable after TopToolbar 64 + TabBar 96). With current chrome (164px) + dock (280px), that leaves 206px for the flex-1 region. 90px mirror in 206px is a 44% void. Expanding dock to 280–350px is NG (shrinks the mirror/controls view). CLEANEST FIX: replace the void with a scrollable column of upcoming cues + recent undo actions + quick stats, so the entire console feels 'full' and the operator never scrolls mid-game."

patterns: SPLIT TAP-STAGE (two team halves) — the single most common full-screen scorekeeper layout: the body is divided left/right (or HOME-top/AWAY-bottom in portrait) into two large tap zones, one per team, so each team's +score is a giant edge-anchored target reachable without moving the hand (Virtual Scoreboard, Game Grader's edge-placement principle, basketball head-to-head views). Big number + big +/- per side; the whole half is the button.

STICKY SCORE HEADER + SCROLLABLE/SEGMENTED BODY + PINNED PRIMARY DOCK — a three-band vertical stack that fills the viewport: (1) a compact always-visible score/clock/period header pinned top, (2) a flexible middle that holds the current task's controls, (3) the most-used actions pinned in the bottom thumb dock. The middle band must hold real controls, never be an empty gap (this is exactly the void the current console has between MobileScoreMirror and MobileScoreDock).

BOTTOM PRIMARY DOCK in the thumb zone — frequently-used actions live in a fixed footer because the bottom edges are the comfortable one-handed reach for navigation/primary actions; infrequent actions go up top. Caveat from NN/G and thumb-zone research: the MIDDLE of the screen is actually the most universally tappable area across grips, so the single hottest targets (team +score) can be big and centered-vertically while the dock holds clock + secondary cues.

SEGMENTED / TABBED BODY — instead of one long scroll, the body switches between a few panels via a segmented control or tab strip (Score | Cues/Celebrate | Roster/Spotlight | Ribbon, and a role switch Scorekeeper/Show-Caller/PA). Each panel fills the same body region full-bleed; only one is visible at a time so nothing is hidden behind a mid-game scroll and the screen is always full.

PER-SPORT / PER-ROLE DEDICATED FULL-SCREEN LAYOUTS — leading controllers (Daktronics All Sport, Live Score Remote, Swimmingly) build a UNIQUE full-screen layout per sport AND per operator role rather than one generic board, which is how they eliminate wasted space: every pixel is a control that this sport/role actually needs (basketball gets +1/+2/+3; judged sports get a results grid; PA gets spotlight only).

SWIPE / EXPANDABLE BOTTOM SHEET for secondary depth — a non-modal bottom sheet (or swipe-between-panels) holds secondary actions one gesture away while the primary score surface stays visible; it can expand to full-screen for deeper tasks (roster, share-to-device QR) then collapse back. Rules: never stack sheets, always give an explicit close, don't bury a PRIMARY action in a sheet (NN/G).

ONE-TAP HOT ACTIONS + HOLD-TO-CONFIRM ON DESTRUCTIVE — the 2-3 most-used actions (score each team, start/stop clock) are always one tap in reach with NO confirmation; destructive/irreversible actions (end game, reset, segment change) get a confirm popup or hold-to-confirm so a fat-finger can't wreck the game (Game Grader, the console's existing HoldChip).

EDGE-ANCHORED HIGH-FREQUENCY TARGETS, MINIMIZE HAND TRAVEL — place the highest-frequency taps on the screen edges / corners the resting thumb already covers so the operator never repositions their grip mid-play; keep targets >=44px (score buttons bigger), with visible press feedback since iOS gives no haptic from navigator.vibrate.

FILL WITH dvh/svh + SAFE-AREA, NOT 100vh — size the full-bleed controller to the dynamic/small viewport (prefer svh for the stable bulk of layout, dvh only where tested) and pad the bottom dock with env(safe-area-inset-bottom) so nothing hides under the home indicator or the iOS URL bar as it animates; promote slide/overlay panels with will-change/contain.

PROGRESSIVE DISCLOSURE OF CHROME — collapse/auto-hide the management chrome (the SWITCH-VIEW pill row, GAME-STATE row, SCREENS health row) on mobile into a compact strip or a top-sheet so it stops eating vertical space; surface it on demand, keep the live controls maximized by default.
understand.recommendation:
For a web React full-bleed one-handed live game controller at 375-430px, combine four patterns into a single dvh/svh-tall flex column that the mobile (md:hidden) subtree owns end-to-end, replacing today's top-sliver-MobileScoreMirror + bottom-MobileScoreDock + empty-void layout:

1) STICKY SCORE HEADER (top, compact ~64-80px): promote MobileScoreMirror to a slim sticky header showing HOME score / clock+segment / AWAY score + game-state chip (Live/Halftime/Final). Collapse the SWITCH-VIEW pills, GAME-STATE row and SCREENS health row OFF the always-on mobile flow into this header's overflow (a tap opens a top/bottom sheet) so they stop eating height. This kills the wasted vertical band.

2) SEGMENTED BODY (flex-1, fills the void): put a segmented control / tab strip under the header — Score | Celebrate | Roster | Ribbon (driven by the existing role view: Scorekeeper/Show-Caller/PA). Each tab renders ONE full-bleed panel into the flex-1 region so there is never an empty middle and never a mid-game scroll. Default tab = the SPLIT TAP-STAGE: two big team halves (HOME / AWAY) each a large +score target with per-sport increments (basketball +1/+2/+3) and a small -1, sized to fill the middle — this is where the wasted space goes. Judged/leaderboard sports swap this panel for the results grid. Celebrate tab holds the GOAL/Save/Exclusion/Power-Play/Horn launchpad; Roster tab the spotlight; Ribbon tab the awareness preview.

3) PERSISTENT BOTTOM DOCK (thumb zone, pinned, safe-area padded): keep the clock Start/Stop as the single biggest always-visible action plus segment +/- and timeout — the controls needed in EVERY tab — so clock control is one tap regardless of which panel is open. Reuse the existing ctl mutations (no data-layer change).

4) DEPTH VIA NON-MODAL BOTTOM SHEET, not a scroll: Send-to-device QR, end-game, and reset live in a swipe-up sheet with explicit close + hold-to-confirm on the destructive ones (NN/G: never bury a primary action, never stack sheets, guard destructive taps).

This is the cross-app consensus shape (Daktronics/Live-Score per-sport full panel + Virtual Scoreboard split tap-stage + the universal sticky-header/segmented-body/bottom-dock three-band) and it keeps ALL functionality reachable one-handed with zero wasted space. Scope every change to the md:hidden subtree; the only OUTER RunMode change to flag for the lead is gating the SWITCH-VIEW/GAME-STATE/SCREENS rows behind md: (or moving them into the new mobile header sheet) so they don't render in the mobile flow — desktop (md+) stays untouched. Use svh for the column height with dvh-tested fallback, env(safe-area-inset-bottom) on the dock, and will-change/contain on the tab/sheet transitions per the mobile-perf standard (no new pollers, breakpoint-gate any backdrop-blur)."}
